NULL at whole-op DEVICE KERNEL DURATION level for all 4 correct variants across all 5 shapes (all within +-8% noise band, several reruns taken). At the writer_issue zone level: addr_recurrence flat-to-mildly-worse everywhere (division was already a compile-time-const-divisor magic-multiply, not naive division, so nothing to save); coord_reuse_raw reproducibly WORSE on wide_short (+16-24% across 2 runs) and tall_narrow (noisy, small absolute ns); combined inherits both, net flat-to-worse. set_state_naive is INCORRECT (xfail, wrong DRAM bank) AND ~4.2x slower (bank-hotspot convergence). Decisive fabric-vs-RISC test: focus-shape per-core geometry (8 writes) at 64-cores-active = 542 ns/write vs 1-core-active = 68 ns/write -- 8x collapse proves the ~540ns/call issue cost the coordinator measured is NoC/DRAM fabric back-pressure from 64 cores sharing 12 banks, not RISC-side command-programming cost. That is the root cause every state-reuse variant is a null/regression: the lever only touches the ~68ns uncontended RISC slice (13% of the total), and the correctness-required noc_cmd_buf_ready guard my raw-LLK variant needed ate even that. Writing final report now.

reader_bank_rotate = WIN on the reader stage in isolation (reads-only ablation TILIZE_ABLATE=writes,compute, 2 reps median): focus shape attention NCRISC mean 5545->4769ns (-14.0%) max 7139->6178ns (-13.5%); short_wide_wide -6.7%/-4.9%; width_chunked -7.7%/-8.9%; square_mid FLAT (+0.8%/-2.3%, partial lockstep); tall_narrow FLAT (-2.2%/-2.2%, disjoint per-core ranges, matches mechanism prediction of no lockstep to fix). raw-loop-vs-helper control (variant1, r0=0) gave ~0-2% alone, confirming the rotation itself (not bypassing the helper) is the mechanism. All rotation strides {1,5,7,11,13} and the bank-exact formula (variant3) win by statistically the same ~13-18%, no ordering by stride -- recommend stride=1 (reuses w_chunk directly, zero extra derivation, cheapest). Spread (max/mean NCRISC) stays ~1.03-1.3x across baseline AND rotated variants per shape -- rotation moves mean+tail down PROPORTIONALLY, does not disproportionately flatten the tail. Whole-op DEVICE KERNEL DURATION barely moves (attention -2.1%, others within +-3%) because BRISC(writer) KERNEL span stays flat (~9900-10100ns) regardless of reader variant -- writer dominates wall on this op structure (matches shared context: writes 55% share vs reads 33%), so the reader win is real but currently hidden by the writer bottleneck; flagging for coordinator that writer_bank_rotate/other writer-side wins would be needed to surface this in the whole-op number.
